business_problem: IRC teams needed to analyze frontline health data quickly enough to influence staffing, outreach, and supplies, but the information came from ministry-run facilities in inconsistent paper and Excel formats and often had to be used in low-connectivity environments.
solution_summary: IRC used Claude Enterprise to create a lightweight offline analytics workflow instead of trying to standardize every upstream data source. In Burkina Faso, staff compile aggregate facility data into Excel and drag those files into a single HTML dashboard template generated and refined with Claude. The template covers more than 15 core health and reproductive-health indicators, runs locally without coding or internet connectivity, and keeps data off Claude's servers. Because the dashboard is just one portable HTML file, measurement specialists and health teams can adapt it in natural language instead of waiting for engineers. The same locally loaded data then supports cross-facility trend analysis, portfolio-level synthesis, and investigations into service gaps, outreach effects, or emerging infection spikes.

solution_components.name: Claude Enterprise
solution_components.role: Generates and iterates the offline HTML dashboard workflow used by frontline health teams.

data_flow: Facility data moves from paper registers or DHIS-2 into local Excel files, staff drag those files into an HTML dashboard template generated with Claude, and the offline output surfaces indicator trends and anomalies for health teams to discuss and act on locally.
business_outcome: IRC reduced management-ready analysis from a full working day to under 30 minutes, saved every surveyed pilot user time, and used the dashboards to validate youth outreach, uncover prenatal-care gaps, and catch infection trends early enough to adjust staffing and supplies.
